message.content:
A worm wheel for an electric power steering system is a gear used in a steering column assembly. The candidate headings are:

- 8483.40 covers gears and gearing, including worm gears, so a worm wheel could fall here.
- 8708.94 covers steering wheels, steering columns and steering boxes, plus parts thereof, for motor vehicles. 8708.94.71 is the parts provision, and 8708.94.75 covers other parts.

The question is whether the worm wheel is a part of a steering system or a general-purpose gear. Section XVII Note 2 excludes parts of general use, and Note 2(b) excludes machinery of Section XVI (heading 8483). Heading 8483 covers transmission shafts, gears, and gearing, so Note 2(f) of Section XVII points to 8483 for that class of goods. CBP rulings on worm wheels for EPS have classified them in 8483.40.5010 or 8483.40.5090.

The relevant subheadings are:

- 8483.40.10 covers ball or roller screws.
- 8483.40.50 covers "Gears and gearing, other" at the 6-digit level, which falls under 8483.40.
- 8483.40.5010 is for machine tool gearing, and 8483.40.5090 is for other.

The 8483.40.50 breakout is "Torque converters and speed changers other than…"? Under 8483.40.51 comes "Gear boxes...", and 8483.40.70 is "Other." Rather than rely on those, I recall the statistical structure as 8483.40.10 ball or roller screw, 8483.40.30 Gears and gearing (machinery?), 8483.40.50 Torque converters, and 8483.40.70 Other. Under that, a worm wheel would be 8483.40.5000 or 8483.40.7000. Since the item is a gear rather than a gearbox, the best fit is "Other", 8483.40.70.

The HTS 8483.40 breakdown that I believe applies is:
- 8483.40.10: Ball or roller screw
- 8483.40.30: Gearboxes? (Speed changers)
- 8483.40.50: Torque converters
- 8483.40.70: Other

I'll go with 8483.40.7000.

{"hts_code": "8483.40.7000", "reason": "A worm wheel is a gear, so it is classified as gearing in heading 8483.40; Section XVII Note 2 excludes it from the vehicle steering parts in 8708."}
